items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: So my friend Ross Konikoff played trumpet on “Cats” for twenty years.

ctx.x: So that’s one thing that you might have turned down for musical reasons, to get on, you know get in “Phantom of the Opera” pit and all your financial worries are taken care of.

I subbed down there a couple of nights actually, playing bass trombone. And the music was wonderful oh my goodness, yes. But you know going back to the question you asked me earlier in the interview about turning down jobs, yeah I never, I had the opportunity to do Broadway shows and I never did because I just knew it wasn’t for me. There’s nothing wrong with that, all my friends were playing Broadway shows and they’re paying their rent and supporting their families, and it’s honorable. And some of the new shows…

so there’s a lot of — you know there’s good stuff going on. So my friend Ross Konikoff played trumpet on “Cats” for twenty years. So you know it’s all kinds — all kinds of different music, all kinds of different professional opportunities. Young musicians that come out of college that come to New York and that’s what they want to do is play a Broadway show, and a lot of them are woodwind players that learn to play a lot of different instruments because they knew that was a requirement to play on Broadway.
